rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity should recognize and thank God for creating, teaching, and honoring it, yet instead it deviates from that obligation.
rows.anchor: من مقتضيات تلك الحقيقة : حقيقة أن الله هو الذي خلق .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is also the source who gave the transgressor wealth, as well as his creation, honor, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: كما أنه هو الذي خلقه وأكرمه وعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity generally, except those whom faith protects, fails to thank God when enriched or recognize Him as the source of its gifts, then transgresses.
rows.anchor: لا يشكر حين يعطى فيستغني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth should prompt recognition and gratitude, whereas people instead become rebellious, excessive, boastful, and arrogant.
rows.anchor: من حيث كان ينبغي أن يعرف ثم يشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God is a veiled threat to the one who transgresses and imagines himself self-sufficient: where could he flee?
rows.anchor: فأين يذهب هذا الذي طغى واستغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person and matter ultimately returns to God: righteous and wicked, obedient and disobedient, right and wrong, rich and poor.
rows.anchor: الرجعة إليه في كل شيء وفي كل أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faith-based conception joins creation, human honor and teaching, and the final return to God alone, without a partner.
rows.anchor: التكريم والتعليم .  .  ثم .  .  الرجعة والمآب لله وحده بلا شريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's third movement depicts an appalling instance of tyranny and expresses astonishment at its occurrence.
rows.anchor: يعرض صورة من صور الطغيان : صورة مستنكرة يعجب منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its denunciation and wonder are conveyed through a distinctive live-address style of quick, broken touches, difficult to reproduce in writing.
rows.anchor: والتشنيع والتعجيب واضح في طريقة التعبير ،  التي تتعذر مجاراتها في لغة الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question makes listeners witness the scandalous act, then intensifies it by adding one ugliness and brutality to another.
rows.anchor: أرأيت حين تضم شناعة إلى شناعة ? وتضاف بشاعة إلى بشاعة ?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshiper may be guided, yet the forbidding person still tries to stop him, even though he is guided and commands piety.
rows.anchor: مع أنه على الهدى ،  آمر بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is especially outrageous if the worshiper himself is guided and urges others toward piety.
rows.anchor: مع أنه على الهدى ،  آمر بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question adds a second, even more reprehensible act to the original offense: denial and turning away.
rows.anchor: أضاف إلى الفعلة المستنكرة فعلة أخرى أشد نكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees the opponent's denial and turning away and his attempt to stop a believing worshiper who is guided and urges piety; this is an implicit threat.
rows.anchor: يرى تكذيبه وتوليه .  ويرى نهيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage now gives an explicit, decisive final threat against tyranny directed at the call, faith, and obedience.
rows.anchor: وأمام مشهد الطغيان الذي يقف في وجه الدعوة وفي وجه الإيمان ،  وفي وجه الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safʿ means seizing violently; the forehead is the arrogant tyrant's raised, forward, conspicuous part.
rows.anchor: والسفع :  الأخذ بعنف .  والناصية :  الجبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat's severe sound portrays the violence of the seizure it threatens.
rows.anchor: بهذا اللفظ الشديد المصور بجرسه لمعناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This lying, sinful forehead deserves to be seized and cast down; the wording evokes the moment of violent seizure and overthrow.
rows.anchor: إنها ناصية تستحق السفع والصرع :  ( ناصية كاذبة خاطئة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrogant man may think to call on the family and companions in whom he takes pride for support.
rows.anchor: فقد يخطر له أن يدعو من يعتز بهم من أهله وصحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will summon the stern, harsh Zabaniya, so the outcome of the confrontation is already known.
rows.anchor: أما نحن فإننا ( سندع الزبانية )الشداد الغلاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer must not obey the tyrant who forbids prayer and the call; he should prostrate, draw near to God through worship, and leave the tyrant to the Zabaniya.
rows.anchor: لا تطع هذا الطاغي الذي ينهى عن الصلاة والدعوة .  واسجد لربك

rows.speaker: الروايات الصحيحة
rows.claim: Sound reports say all but the surah's opening passage was revealed about Abu Jahl after he saw Muhammad praying at the Maqam and forbade him.
rows.anchor: وردت بعض الروايات الصحيحة بأن السورة - عدا المقطع الأول منها - قد نزلت في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb suggests this may be the occasion when the Prophet seized Abu Jahl by the collar and rebuked him; Abu Jahl replied by boasting of his powerful council.
rows.anchor: وقال له : أولى لك ثم أولى فقال : يا محمد بأي شي تهددني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that had Abu Jahl called his council, the angels of punishment would have seized him immediately.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس لو دعا ناديه لأخذته ملائكة العذاب من ساعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning applies generally to every obedient believer who worships and calls to God, and every arrogant aggressor who forbids prayer and threatens obedience.
rows.anchor: وكل طاغ باغ ينهى عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and contains five verses.
rows.anchor: سورة القدر مكية وآياتها خمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night marks the joyful cosmic meeting of earth and the heavenly assembly, when the Qur'an first descended into Muhammad's heart, an unprecedented event in human history.
rows.anchor: ليلة الاتصال المطلق بين الأرض والملأ الأعلى .  ليلة بدء نزول هذا القرآن على قلب محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the blessed night named in 44:3–6, and it is known to be in Ramadan, as 2:185 states; the Qur'an's descent began then for the Messenger to deliver it.
rows.anchor: والمعروف أنها ليلة من ليالي رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that the opening of Surat al-Alaq was the first revelation, in Ramadan, while Muhammad was worshiping in the cave of Hira.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية ابن إسحاق أن أول الوحي بمطلع سورة العلق كان في شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place the night variously on Ramadan's twenty-seventh or twenty-first, within its final ten nights, or anywhere in Ramadan; the strongest reports place it in Ramadan generally.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في تعيين هذه الليلة آثار كثيرة .  بعضها يعين الليلة السابعة والعشرين من رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr may mean divine determination and management, or worth and rank; both meanings suit the immense event of Qur'an, revelation, and messengership.
rows.anchor: قد يكون معناه التقدير والتدبير .  وقد يكون معناه القيمة والمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The number one thousand months is not a precise limit here but signals abundance: many thousands of months and years left less impact than this night.
rows.anchor: والعدد لا يفيد التحديد .  في مثل هذه المواضع من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is too great for human understanding, without needing the myths circulated in popular imagination; God's choice of it to begin revelation made it great.
rows.anchor: وذلك بدون حاجة إلى التعلق بالأساطير التي شاعت حول هذه الليلة في أوهام العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its greatness lies in the Qur'an's light reaching all existence, the peace flowing from God's spirit into human conscience and life, and the Qur'an's creed, conception, law, and manners.
rows.anchor: وإسباغ السلام الذي فاض من روح الله على الضمير البشري والحياة الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the blessed night named in 44:3–6, and it is known to be in Ramadan, as 2:185 states; the Qur'an's descent began then for the Messenger to deliver it.
rows.anchor: والمعروف أنها ليلة من ليالي رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that the opening of Surat al-Alaq was the first revelation, in Ramadan, while Muhammad was worshiping in the cave of Hira.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية ابن إسحاق أن أول الوحي بمطلع سورة العلق كان في شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place the night variously on Ramadan's twenty-seventh or twenty-first, within its final ten nights, or anywhere in Ramadan; the strongest reports place it in Ramadan generally.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في تعيين هذه الليلة آثار كثيرة .  بعضها يعين الليلة السابعة والعشرين من رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadr may mean divine determination and management, or worth and rank; both meanings suit the immense event of Qur'an, revelation, and messengership.
rows.anchor: قد يكون معناه التقدير والتدبير .  وقد يكون معناه القيمة والمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The number one thousand months is not a precise limit here but signals abundance: many thousands of months and years left less impact than this night.
rows.anchor: والعدد لا يفيد التحديد .  في مثل هذه المواضع من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night changed human life more than thousands of months or years, through the immense effects and transformations it set in motion.
rows.anchor: فكم من آلاف الشهور وآلاف السنين قد انقضت دون أن تترك في الحياة بعض ما تركته هذه الليلة المباركة السعيدة من آثار وتحولات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels, especially Gabriel, descend by their Lord's permission, accompanied by the Qur'an in the sense of the revelation's kind, and spread between heaven and earth in a cosmic festival.
rows.anchor: وانتشارهم فيما بين السماء والأرض في هذا المهرجان الكوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That night established values and foundations and determined destinies larger than those of individuals: nations, states, peoples, facts, conditions, and hearts.
rows.anchor: وقد وضعت فيها من قيم وأسس وموازين .  وقد قررت فيها من أقدار أكبر من أقدار الأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's forgetfulness of the night made it lose God's happiest gift and genuine peace in conscience, home, and society; material prosperity and civilization cannot replace it.
rows.anchor: فقدت أسعد وأجمل آلاء الله عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity also lost the spiritual joy, heavenly light, and peace that once flowed into human hearts; nothing compensates for that loss.
rows.anchor: فلم يعوضها شيء عن فرحة الروح ونور السماء وطلاقة الرفرفة إلى عليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet urged Muslims to seek the Night of Decree in Ramadan's final ten nights, as reported in both Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: تحروا ليلة القدر في العشر الأواخر من رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet promised forgiveness of past sins for one who stands in prayer on the Night of Decree with faith and seeking reward.
rows.anchor: من قام ليلة القدر إيمانا واحتسابا غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and seeking reward make the vigil revive the night’s great meanings and embody sincere devotion to God, rather than mere outward form.
rows.anchor: وذلك ليكون هذا القيام استحياء للمعاني الكبيرة التي اشتملت عليها هذه الليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islamic education joins worship to creed in the conscience, making belief vivid in feeling and action; theoretical understanding without worship does not establish or energize it.
rows.anchor: المنهج الإسلامي في التربية يربط بين العبادة وحقائق العقيدة في الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linking remembrance of the Night of Decree with prayer on it exemplifies this effective Islamic method of education.
rows.anchor: وهذا الربط بين ذكرى ليلة القدر وبين القيام فيها إيمانا واحتسابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Madinan according to most reports, though some say Meccan; Qutb favors Madinan on the basis of reports and its declarative style but does not rule out a Meccan origin.
rows.anchor: فإن كونها مكية لا يمكن استبعاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of the People of the Book and zakah does not exclude a Meccan origin: some People of the Book lived in Mecca, Najran Christians visited and believed, and zakah appears in Meccan surahs.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزكاة فيها وذكر أهل الكتاب لا يعتبر قرينة مانعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's four central truths are that the final Messenger's mission was necessary, the People of the Book divided after proof, religion's core is simple and one, and the disbelievers and believers face different fates.
rows.anchor: كانت ضرورية لتحويل الذين كفروا من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth had become deeply corrupt, with both scriptural communities having distorted earlier religions and polytheism widespread; only a new message, method, and movement could bring reform.
rows.anchor: لقد كانت الأرض في حاجة ماسة إلى رسالة جديدة كان الفساد قد عم أرجاءها كلها بحيث لا يرتجى لها صلاح إلا برسالة جديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those disbelievers would not abandon their condition without the new message and a Messenger who himself served as a decisive, clear proof.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا لينفكوا ويتحولوا عن هذا الكفر الذي صاروا إليه إلا بهذه الرسالة الجديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger comes from God and recites purified scriptures; the scriptures are purified of associating partners with God and unbelief.
rows.anchor: مطهرة من الشرك والكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitab can mean a subject or topic, as in chapters on purification, prayer, divine decree, and resurrection; the Qur'an's purified pages contain valuable topics and truths.
rows.anchor: كما يقال كتاب الطهارة وكتاب الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book split after receiving knowledge and clear proof through their messengers, not because their religion was obscure or complicated.
rows.anchor: إنما هم تفرقوا واختلفوا من بعد ما جاءهم العلم ومن بعد ما جاءتهم البينة من دينهم على أيدي رسلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earliest division was among Jews before Jesus: although they shared Moses and the Torah, they formed five principal sects, including Sadducees, Pharisees, Essenes, zealots, and Samaritans.
rows.anchor: وكان أول التفرق والاختلاف ما وقع بين طوائف اليهود قبل بعثة عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jewish-Christian division became violent despite Jesus being an Israelite prophet who affirmed the Torah; history preserved massacres between the two communities.
rows.anchor: ثم كان التفرق بين اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A historical account says Jews attacked Christians at Antioch near the end of Phocas's reign in 610; the Byzantine commander answered with exceptionally cruel mass killings.
rows.anchor: في السنة الأخيرة من حكم فوكاس

rows.speaker: المقريزي
rows.claim: Al-Maqrizi recounts Persian forces destroying churches and killing Christians, with Jewish assistance, followed by Heraclius's oath to spare the Jews and later massacre of them after Christian clergy advised him to expiate the oath by annual fasting.
rows.anchor: قال المقريزي في كتاب الخطط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These accounts show both Jews and Christians had reached extreme cruelty, seeking opportunities to harm enemies without respecting limits.
rows.anchor: من القسوة والضراوة بالدم الإنساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Christians later divided among themselves over doctrine, then became hostile sects debating Christ's nature, Mary's nature, and the Trinity; the Qur'an cites examples of their claims.
rows.anchor: وقد دارت الخلافات حول طبيعة المسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Melkites held a dual nature for Christ, while Egyptian Monophysites held one divine nature in which the human nature vanished; by the sixth and seventh centuries the dispute resembled a war between rival religions.
rows.anchor: فكان شعار الملكانية عقيدة ازدواج طبيعة المسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heraclius tried to reconcile the factions by imposing one divine will as a state doctrine; the Copts rejected the innovation, and a later compromise did not calm the dispute.
rows.anchor: وصار المذهب المنوثيلي مذهبا رسميا للدولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute led to ten years of brutal Egyptian persecution, including drowning, burning, and other torture.
rows.anchor: ووقع اضطهاد فظيع على يد قيصر في مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these disagreements arose after the People of the Book had received proof; lack of knowledge was not the problem, but desire and deviation swept them away.
rows.anchor: إنما كان يجرفهم الهوى والانحراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion's universal foundation is worshiping God alone, sincerely devoting religion to Him, turning away from polytheism, establishing prayer, and giving zakah.
rows.anchor: عبادة الله وحده ،  وإخلاص الدين له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith comprises sincere belief in the heart, worship expressing that belief, and giving wealth for God's sake; these are the faith required of the People of the Book and all religion.
rows.anchor: عقيدة خالصة في الضمير ،  وعبادة لله ،  تترجم عن هذه العقيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion is one across successive revelations and messengers, clear and easy, not a cause of complexity, division, or endless disputation.
rows.anchor: دين لا غموض فيه ولا تعقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proof came through earlier messengers and then the final Messenger, the paths and outcomes of belief and unbelief are clear: the disbelievers are consigned to enduring Hell.
rows.anchor: فأما وقد جاءتهم البينة من قبل في دياناتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last Messenger and Islam are the final, comprehensive message; after earlier repeated opportunities to reform, humanity now faces its last opportunity: belief brings salvation and unbelief ruin.
rows.anchor: إن محمدا [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] هو الرسول الأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelief after the final proof signifies boundless evil, while faith signifies the furthest reach of good; this is a categorical judgment.
rows.anchor: ذلك أن الكفر حينئذ دلالة على الشر الذي لا حد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No good works, manners, or social systems can change the judgment when detached from faith in this final message and its final Messenger.
rows.anchor: مهما يكن من صلاح بعض أعمالهم وآدابهم ونظمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being born in a Muslim land or family, or merely using religious words, does not meet the clear condition of faith.
rows.anchor: لا مجرد مولد في أرض تدعى الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True faith produces effects in life; good deeds include every act of worship, moral conduct, work, and dealings that God commands, foremost establishing God's law and judging by it.
rows.anchor: إنه الإيمان الذي ينشئ آثاره في واقع الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who combine faith with such deeds are the best of creation.
rows.anchor: فمن كانوا كذلك فهم خير البرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise offers lasting residence, safety from extinction and loss, freedom from earthly anxiety, and rivers that evoke freshness, life, and beauty.
rows.anchor: في نعيمها الذي يمثله هنا الأمن من الفناء والفوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's pleasure is higher and sweeter than every other bliss; believers' contentment with His decree, gifts, and bond with them brings profound calm and joy.
rows.anchor: هذا الرضا من الله وهو أعلى وأندى من كل نعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reward depends on a heart connected to God and reverent fear that drives righteousness and blocks deviation.
rows.anchor: التوكيد على أن هذا كله متوقف على صلة القلب بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True reverence purifies worship and action from showing off and every form of association; God rejects work in which the servant looks to another alongside Him.
rows.anchor: والذي يخلص العبادة ويخلص العمل من شوائب الرياء والشرك في كل صورة من صوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's four great truths are presented through the Qur'an's distinctive style, especially in its short chapters.
rows.anchor: تلك الحقائق الأربعة الكبيرة هي مقررات هذه السورة الصغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the printed Qur'an and some reports classify the surah as Madinan, other reports call it Meccan; Qutb prefers the Meccan reports because its style and subject support them.
rows.anchor: ونحن نرجح الروايات التي تقول بأنها مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah shakes heedless hearts with its subject, scene, and rhythm, then swiftly confronts people with judgment, weighing, and recompense.
rows.anchor: إنها هزة عنيفة للقلوب الغافلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene is the Resurrection, when the earth people thought stable trembles violently.
rows.anchor: إنه يوم القيامة حيث ترتجف الأرض الثابتة ارتجافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth shakes out the bodies, minerals, and other burdens it has carried, as if relieving itself of their long weight.
rows.anchor: وتخرج ما يثقلها من أجساد ومعادن وغيرها مما حملته طويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene shakes the listener's sense of stability, making the ground seem to sway; Qur'anic phrasing gives its imagined motion a visceral force.
rows.anchor: مشهد يخلع القلوب من كل ما تتشبث به من هذه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human depicted is stunned and bewildered, asking what is happening to the earth and seeking something stable to hold onto.
rows.anchor: وهو سؤال المشدوه المبهوت المفجوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People have experienced terrifying earthquakes and volcanoes, but the Resurrection's upheaval is wholly new, without a known cause or precedent.
rows.anchor: ولكنه حين يرى زلزال يوم القيامة لا يجد أن هناك شبها بينه وبين ما كان يقع من الزلازل والبراكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day the earth tells what happened to it, describing its condition and events.
rows.anchor: وتصف حالها وما جرى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded the earth to quake, move, and release its burdens; it obeyed, and its state plainly reports God's command and revelation.
rows.anchor: وأمرها أن تمور مورا ،  وأن تزلزل زلزالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shocked human is then confronted with the gathering, judgment, weighing, and recompense.
rows.anchor: هنا يواجه بمشهد الحشر والحساب والوزن والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People emerge from graves in separate groups, like scattered locusts, then hurry toward the caller with stretched necks and fixed eyes, each absorbed in personal concerns.
rows.anchor: نرى مشهدهم شتيتا منبعثا من أرجاء الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They go to be shown their deeds and face their consequences; simply seeing one's past work, especially before all and before God, can be a punishment more painful than other requital.
rows.anchor: إنهم ذاهبون إلى حيث تعرض عليهم أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's exact accounting weighs and requites every trace of good or evil, so no deed can be dismissed as too small to count.
rows.anchor: الحساب الدقيق الذي لا يدع ذرة من خير أو من شر لا يزنها ولا يجازي عليها

rows.speaker: المفسرون القدامى
rows.claim: Earlier commentators identified a dharrah as a mosquito or as a mote visible in sunlight, the smallest things they could imagine.
rows.anchor: كان المفسرون القدامى يقولون : إنها البعوضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb says modern science identifies the atom, much smaller than a mote, as invisible even under powerful microscopes and known through its effects.
rows.anchor: فنحن الآن نعلم أن الذرة شيء محدد يحمل هذا الإسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A weight like an atom of good or evil will appear before its doer, who will receive its recompense.
rows.anchor: فهذه أو ما يشبهها من ثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The precise scale should make people tremble before every deed; the believer's heart responds to even an atom's weight, while other hearts ignore mountains of sin or good.
rows.anchor: القلب الذي يرتعش لمثقال ذرة من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hard hearts are weighed down by their loads of wrongdoing on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: إنها قلوب عتلة في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's exact accounting weighs and requites every trace of good or evil, so no deed can be dismissed as too small to count.
rows.anchor: الحساب الدقيق الذي لا يدع ذرة من خير أو من شر لا يزنها ولا يجازي عليها

rows.anchor: فهذه أو ما يشبهها من ثقل

rows.anchor: القلب الذي يرتعش لمثقال ذرة من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hard hearts are weighed down by their loads of wrongdoing on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: إنها قلوب عتلة في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The horses reach the enemy's ranks by surprise, causing confusion and disorder; this depicts battle steps familiar to the first Qur'anic audience.
rows.anchor: وهي تتوسط صفوف الأعداء على غرة فتوقع بينهم الفوضى والاضطراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's image values the horses' movement and activity before God and fits the scene with the truths that follow.
rows.anchor: والقسم بالخيل في هذا الإطار فيه إيحاء قوي بحب هذه الحركة والنشاط لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next oath concerns the ingratitude rooted in a human heart emptied of faith; the Qur'an alerts people to it so they can struggle against it.
rows.anchor: أما الذي يقسم الله - سبحانه - عليه ،  فهو حقيقة في نفس الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being may testify to this truth against himself, or may testify on Judgment Day to his own ingratitude when denial is no longer possible.
rows.anchor: وكأنه يشهد على نفسه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without faith, a person loves himself intensely and therefore loves worldly wealth, power, and pleasures as he imagines them.
rows.anchor: فهو شديد الحب لنفسه ،  ومن ثم يحب الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith transforms his priorities, turning ingratitude into gratitude and selfishness and greed into generosity and mercy, and reveals values greater than worldly possessions.
rows.anchor: فيغير من تصوراته وقيمه وموازينه واهتماماته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without faith, human ambition remains petty, earthbound, limited by lifespan and trapped in the self; connection to God and the Hereafter alone liberates it.
rows.anchor: ومهما كبرت أطماعه .  واشتد طموحه ،  وتعالت أهدافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith connects earthly life to an eternal world from God, the Everlasting Origin, and returning to God, the Everlasting End.
rows.anchor: عالم يصدر عن الله الأزلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final reminder confronts ingratitude, selfishness, and greed with Resurrection, breaking self-interest and awakening people from heedlessness.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم تجيء اللفتة الأخيرة في السورة لعلاج الكنود والجحود والأثرة والشح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The graves are violently scattered in a forceful scene designed to unsettle the audience.
rows.anchor: وهو مشهد عنيف مثير .  بعثرة لما في القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden secrets people concealed in their hearts are extracted in a harsh, violent scene.
rows.anchor: وتحصيل لأسرار الصدور التي ضنت بها وخبأتها بعيدا عن العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question leaves its object unstated because the Resurrection alone is enough to shake the heart, which is left to imagine the consequences.
rows.anchor: ولا يذكر ماذا يعلم ? لأن علمه بهذا وحده يكفي لهز المشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All matters and fates return to their Lord, who knows people and their inward states; though God always knows, His knowledge that day carries the consequence of reckoning and requital.
rows.anchor: فالمرجع إلى ربهم .  وإنه لخبير بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's tumultuous movement and rhythm come to rest in this final resolution.
rows.anchor: إن السورة مشوار واحد لاهث صاخب ثائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is Meccan and has eleven verses; Qari'ah means Resurrection, like other names for it, and evokes pounding that strikes hearts with dread.
rows.anchor: والقارعة توحي بالقرع واللطم ،  فهي تقرع القلوب بهولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its scene shows people as scattered moths, confused and directionless, and mountains as teased wool tossed about; the word's sound and image prepare for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: فيبدو الناس في ظله صغارا ضئالا على كثرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah first hurls the lone word without a predicate or description, making its shadow and sound strike with dread.
rows.anchor: لقد بدأ بإلقاء الكلمة مفردة كأنها قذيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The follow-up question amplifies dread by presenting the Resurrection as an awesome, obscure event that provokes astonishment and questioning.
rows.anchor: فهي الأمر المستهول الغامض الذي يثير الدهش والتساؤل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question renders the event beyond human comprehension and imagination.
rows.anchor: فهي أكبر من أن يحيط بها الإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer describes what will happen rather than the event's essence, which remains beyond comprehension; the first scene shakes hearts and limbs.
rows.anchor: ثم الإجابة بما يكون فيها ،  لا بماهيتها .  فماهيتها فوق الإدراك والتصور كما أسلفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene makes listeners feel that everything they grasp on earth has vanished into scattered dust.
rows.anchor: ويحس السامع كأن كل شيء يتشبث به في الأرض قد طار حوله هباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer describes what will happen rather than the event's essence, which remains beyond comprehension; the first scene shakes hearts and limbs.
rows.anchor: ثم الإجابة بما يكون فيها ،  لا بماهيتها .  فماهيتها فوق الإدراك والتصور كما أسلفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene makes listeners feel that everything they grasp on earth has vanished into scattered dust.
rows.anchor: ويحس السامع كأن كل شيء يتشبث به في الأرض قد طار حوله هباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This familiar Qur'anic question deliberately makes people realize their ignorance and dread, since the matter lies beyond imagination and comprehension.
rows.anchor: سؤال التجهيل والتهويل المعهود في القرآن ،  لإخراج الأمر عن حدود التصور وحيز الإدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light-scaled person's supposed refuge is reframed as a mother, normally a place of safety, but it is a deep abyss and blazing fire; the reversal is a sharp expressive surprise.
rows.anchor: والأم عندها الأمن والراحة .  فماذا هو واجد عند أمه هذه .  .  الهاوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After people visit the graves, this warning strikes their hearts with dread about what awaits, in a deep, steady rhythm.
rows.anchor: ثم يقرع قلوبهم بهول ما ينتظرهم هناك بعد زيارة المقابر في إيقاع عميق رزين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the rhythm and wording deepens insistence and dread, hinting at a grave reality they cannot discern amid heedless excess.
rows.anchor: ثم يزيد التوكيد عمقا ورهبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to certain knowledge prepares the audience for the terrible fact concealed behind their heedlessness.
rows.anchor: ثم يكشف عن هذه الحقيقة المطوية الرهيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah now discloses the terrifying fact that people will see the blazing Fire.
rows.anchor: ثم يؤكد هذه الحقيقة ويعمق وقعها الرهيب في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second assertion intensifies the certainty and dread of seeing the Fire.
rows.anchor: ثم يلقي بالإيقاع الأخير ،  الذي يدع المخمور يفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will be questioned about where they obtained their blessings and how they spent them, whether in obedience or sin, lawfully or unlawfully.
rows.anchor: لتسألن عنه من أين نلتموه ? وفيم أنفقتموه ? أمن طاعة وفي طاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be asked whether they thanked God, fulfilled obligations, shared blessings, or monopolized them; what they boast about becomes a heavy burden.
rows.anchor: هل شكرتم ? هل أديتم ? هل شاركتم ? هل استأثرتم ?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's rhythm and meaning turn the heart from trivial worldly concerns toward the Hereafter, reminding it that earthly life is brief but its burdens endure.
rows.anchor: حتى يشعر بثقل ما على عاتقه من أعقاب هذه الحياة الوامضة التي يحياها على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its message moves the listener to examine even small matters and valuables.
rows.anchor: ثم ينشئ يحاسب نفسه على الصغير والزهيد
